content: Perinatal Assistants are professionals who provide comprehensive support during the childbearing period. Their services encompass a combination of doula care, childbirth education, postpartum support, and breastfeeding assistance. The training required to become a Perinatal Assistant involves a minimum of ten months of structured instruction. This training includes in-depth study of anatomy and physiology, the physiology of childbirth, labor support techniques, breastfeeding management, postpartum care, and the development of educational and teaching skills. Additionally, the program requires the completion of a thesis and a final examination. This educational pathway is offered as either a Diploma or an Associate Degree program. At present, the only registered Perinatal Assistant education program is provided by the Global Birth Institute.
